config.title: useWindowSize

intro.title: useWindowSize
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reactive custom composable function called `useWindowSize` that tracks and updates the current width and height of the browser window. You'll learn how to use Vue's `ref` and `onMounted`/`onUnmounted` lifecycle hooks to manage reactive state and side effects. The core concept involves listening to the `resize` event to update the window dimensions in real-time. By the end, you'll have a reusable utility that can be integrated into any Vue component to respond dynamically to window size changes.
intro.usecase: The useWindowSize pattern is essential for creating responsive interfaces that adapt to different screen dimensions. In real applications, you'll use it to conditionally render dashboard components—showing detailed charts on large screens while switching to simplified cards on mobile. E-commerce sites apply this to rearrange product grids, adjusting column counts based on available width. Media players might hide control panels on smaller screens, and data tables often collapse into scrollable views when space is limited. This reactive approach ensures optimal user experience across all devices.

objectives: Implement a reactive window size composable using Vue's ref and onMounted/onUnmounted lifecycle hooks
Construct an event listener that updates reactive values when the window is resized
Initialize and expose width and height values from the composable for component consumption
Integrate the useWindowSize composable into a Vue component template
Manipulate the DOM by conditionally rendering elements based on window size thresholds
Apply the window size data to dynamically control CSS classes or inline styles
Configure cleanup logic to remove event listeners when the component is unmounted

steps.title: Define the updateWindowSize handler function
steps.instruction: Inside the useWindowSize function, define a function named updateWindowSize that updates the width and height refs with the current window dimensions.

steps.expectedOutcome: The useWindowSize function now contains an updateWindowSize handler that can update the reactive width and height values.

steps.title: Set up the resize event listener with onMounted
steps.instruction: Inside the useWindowSize function, call onMounted to add a 'resize' event listener to the window that calls the updateWindowSize function.
steps.hint: Use onMounted(() => { window.addEventListener('resize', updateWindowSize); }) to set up the event listener when the component mounts.
steps.expectedOutcome: The onMounted lifecycle hook is used to attach a resize event listener to the window, which will call updateWindowSize whenever the window size changes.
successCriteria: onMounted is called with a callback that adds a 'resize' event listener to the window, and the listener calls updateWindowSize.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.

steps.feedbackWrong: That's not quite right. You need to use onMounted to add a 'resize' event listener to the window that calls updateWindowSize.

steps.expectedOutcome: The useWindowSize function now returns an object with width and height refs, making these reactive values available to any component that uses this composable.
successCriteria: The useWindowSize function returns an object containing both width and height refs.
